# Incident Report — MTA 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString; domain-joined to SPOONWATCH.NET, DC = SPOONWATCH-DC at 192.168.1.2) |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith (SPOONWATCH domain account, seen authenticating via Kerberos) |

## Malware Family
**Vidar Stealer.** Attribution is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed — no Suricata/IDS alert file was present in the evidence directory (only the pcap), so this is a traffic/artifact-based identification, not a matched IDS rule. Grounds for the ID:

- The malware pulled down seven files disguised with `.jpg` extensions and `Content-Type: image/jpeg`, but each is actually a legitimate PE32 DLL: `freebl3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll`, plus an sqlite3-linked DLL (confirmed via embedded PDB paths, e.g. `...obj-thunderbird\security\nss3.pdb`). This exact bundle is used by Vidar/Arkei-family stealers to load Mozilla NSS to decrypt Firefox/Thunderbird stored credentials on the victim host.
- The stolen-data archive exfiltrated to the C2 unzips (per embedded filenames) into `autofill/`, `cc/` (credit cards), `cookies/`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt` — the standard Vidar stealer-log folder layout.
- HTTP request headers from the infected host carry `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` and a fixed non-browser header set on every C2 request, consistent with the Vidar HTTP client fingerprint.
- The C2 was contacted by hardcoded IP with no preceding DNS lookup, typical of Vidar's config-driven C2 list.

Delivery/initial-access vector is **not observable** in this capture — the first packet to the C2 (frame 1498) appears mid-session with no prior download or spawning process visible in the pcap.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (HTTP, no DNS resolution — hardcoded IP)

**Malicious URLs (all on `2.56.57.108`, single TCP conversation, port 49738 → 80)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` — loader/support DLL downloads (server → victim)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — check-in/beacon
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — stolen-data upload (victim → server)

**Files transferred, disguised as JPEGs, actually PE32 DLLs (downloaded from C2):**
| Filename requested | Actual content | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| /osk//1.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 |
| /osk//2.jpg | freebl3.dll | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba |
| /osk//3.jpg | mozglue.dll | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd |
| /osk//4.jpg | msvcp140.dll | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 |
| /osk//5.jpg | nss3.dll | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 |
| /osk//6.jpg | softokn3.dll | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 |
| /osk//7.jpg | vcruntime140.dll | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d |

**Exfiltrated data (victim → C2, POST /osk/, multipart/form-data, 379,629 bytes):**
- Filename: `_5861695120.zip`
- Contents (from embedded zip entry names): `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`

This represents theft of browser-stored autofill data, saved credit card data, session cookies, saved passwords, Outlook data, a desktop screenshot, and system fingerprint information from the DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 host under user steve.smith.

**Noise excluded from this incident:** traffic to `download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.201/225) and `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` for `am_delta_patch_*.exe` and `*.cab` files is legitimate Windows Defender/Windows Update signature traffic, not malicious.
